More about Bills & Subscriptions

The job nobody wants: knowing what is about to charge you, and what is still charging you for something you stopped using. Tell your agent “the design seat is $59.99 monthly on the 3rd”, or “Netflix is $15.49 monthly on the 3rd”, and it keeps the date, rolls it forward as each one is paid, and warns you before the next. Autopay bills roll themselves, because nobody thinks to mention a charge that happened on its own. Ask what a month costs and get the arithmetic across weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly, done properly. With Email Manager (or another skill that reads your mail) installed, it will go and find the subscriptions you forgot to mention. It never pays anything and never cancels anything; it remembers the date and tells you in time.

More about Card Rewards

Most people carry three cards and use the wrong one most of the time, because nobody remembers which earns what. Add each card once and your agent keeps the rates on its row, so the answer at a register is one line and instant. The part that actually pays for itself is the rotating categories: cards that change their bonus every quarter earn the base rate until you activate them, and almost nobody does. It checks whether yours are switched on, tells you when a quarter has turned, and can go and fetch the new list. It never recommends a card you do not have, never suggests applying for one, and never states a rate it did not read from your own row.

What needs me in Stripe?

Download Archie
More about Revenue Watch

Stripe emails you about every one of these and the emails become weather. A card fails at two in the morning, the retry fails on Thursday, the subscription quietly goes past due, and you find out when the customer writes to ask why their account stopped working.

Connect Stripe with a read-only restricted key and your agent reads the real ledger. Ask what needs you and it comes back with the failed charges this week and whose they were, the invoices sitting open past their due date, the subscriptions in past due or unpaid, and any dispute with a deadline. Ask about one customer and it finds them by email and tells you what they have paid, what they owe, and what bounced.

It can refund a charge, void an invoice and cancel a subscription too, and every one of those is shown to you before it happens. Nothing moves money without you saying yes.

Works with

  • Stripe

Setting up Revenue Watch

  1. Make the key at Stripe, under Developers, API keys, and press Create restricted key. Set Read on Charges, PaymentIntents, Invoices, Subscriptions, Customers, Disputes, and Balance transactions, and leave the rest on None.
  2. That read-only key answers every question here and cannot move a penny. Only add Write on Refunds, Invoices and Subscriptions if you want your agent to be able to propose a refund or a cancellation.
  3. Check whether you are in test mode or live mode when you make the key. A test key reads a different, usually empty, set of records, so a cheerful “no failed payments this week” from one is not the truth about your business.

Made by Otian AI.

Collect my statements

Every add-on is included with Archie.

More about Statement Collector

Every month there is a circuit: nine websites, a login on each, a date range, a download button, and a filename you have to invent. This does the circuit.

It starts from your inbox rather than from a list. The bills already arrive as email, so the sender tells it which accounts you have and the message tells it roughly when each one lands. It proposes what it found, you confirm once and sign in once per site, and after that the list keeps itself: a utility you signed up for last week shows up on its own, and one you canceled stops being asked about.

What you get back is not nine PDFs and a shrug. Each statement is filed where you can find it, the amount is read off the page, and you are told the one thing worth knowing: this bill is higher than usual, this one has a new charge on it, this one did not arrive at all.

It uses each site itself, in a window you can watch (Connections tab, under Computer control), and it stops before anything it cannot undo. It never sees your passwords: you sign in yourself, once per site, in your agent's own browser.

Works with any email account connected on the agent's Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files.

What Statement Collector needs

Needs Computer control turned on, which is off until you switch it on. Your agent works the site in a browser window on your own computer, and you can watch it. It never types a password or a card you pay with, and it asks before pressing anything that finalizes.

Mercury Watch

What the balance actually is, and whether the transfer landed.

Try saying

What's my Mercury balance?

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Mercury Watch

Business banking asks you to keep two numbers in your head. The one on the screen, and the one that will be true once the three things in flight have settled. The gap between them is where a bounced payment lives.

Connect Mercury with a read-only token and your agent reads the real accounts. Ask what the balance is and it gives you both figures and says which is which. Ask what came in this week and it reads the credits, not the net. Ask whether a transfer landed and it tells you whether it has posted or is still pending, which is the question you were actually asking.

Read-only is the right token for all of this, and it is the one that needs nothing else set up. Your agent cannot move money on this connection, whatever anyone asks it.

Works with

  • Mercury

Setting up Mercury Watch

  1. Make the token in Mercury, under Settings, Tokens, and choose Read Only. Read Only answers every question here and needs nothing else set up. A read and write token would make Mercury ask for more, and would let your agent be asked to move money.
  2. Copy the whole token, including the part before the colon. Mercury's tokens start with secret-token: and dropping that first part makes every call fail as if the token were wrong.
  3. Mercury deletes a token that has gone forty-five days without being used. If your agent stops being able to read the account after a quiet stretch, that is why, and a new token fixes it.

Made by Otian AI.

On a day when nothing failed, nothing lapsed and nobody disputed anything, it says nothing at all. That is most days, and it is what makes the message worth reading on the day it arrives.

It reads only. Refunds, voided invoices and cancellations stay things you ask for.

More about Square Keeper

Square knows what came in this week, which invoices are still open, and which customer paid with which card. Finding any of it means opening the dashboard, picking a date range, and reading down a list.

Connect Square and ask instead. “What came in this week?” comes back with the total, how many payments, and the dates it counted. “Who hasn’t paid?” lists the open invoices, overdue ones first, with how late each is. “When does my money land?” reads your payouts.

Say “invoice Dana for the color and cut, $120, due next Wednesday” and your agent finds Dana, drafts the invoice in your Square, and shows you who it goes to, the amount, the due date, and the email address before anything is sent. A refund works the same way: whose payment, how much, and which card it goes back to, and nothing moves until you say yes.

It does not charge cards, cancel an invoice that already went out, or change a booking. Those stay in Square.

Works with

  • Square

Setting up Square Keeper

  1. Sign in at developer.squareup.com with your Square account and make a new application. Name it Archie.
  2. Open it, choose Credentials on the left, and pick Production at the top of the page. A Sandbox token reads a pretend account, not your business.
  3. Under Production access token, press Show, then copy the token.

Statement Round

Each statement, collected the day it is ready.

Runs when anything in statement schedule is due, on the day, checked at 9:00 AM

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Statement Round

Accounts do not share a closing date, so a monthly round is either early for half of them or late for the rest. This watches the date your agent keeps against each account and runs that one when it comes up: the card that closes on the 3rd is collected on the 3rd, and the one that closes on the 27th is left alone until the 27th.

The dates are not yours to keep. Your agent works out when each account's statement lands from the mail that already arrives, writes the date down, and moves it forward every time it collects one. If a bank shifts a cycle, the next statement email shifts with it and so does the date. You can edit any of them on the Knowledge tab, under Lists, in the Statement schedule list, and you will not need to.

A day with nothing due is silent. When something is collected you get the PDF, the amount, and whatever is worth knowing about it: higher than usual, a charge that was not there before, or a statement that should have been ready and was not.

It needs Statement Collector, whose sites you sign in to once each. Nothing here handles a password, and nothing here pays anything.

The Bookkeeper

Numbers first. No lecture attached.

How much did I spend on food last month?$1,043 on food last month. $612 groceries, $431 eating out. Counted from 78 transactions, nothing estimated. That is 22% of the month's spending and $180 above your June food number. Biggest single lever: takeout went from 9 orders to 17. Back to 9 puts roughly $200 a month back.

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about The Bookkeeper

Money talk usually arrives with a lecture attached. This one does not have one. Ask what you spent and you get the figure first, then what it does to the month, then the single change that would move it most, sized. It never calls an amount 'just' anything, never congratulates you for an ordinary week, and never tells you what your spending says about you. It rounds when it is speaking and gives you the cent the moment you ask, and it always says whether a number was counted from real transactions or estimated. When you overspend it states the amount and how much room is left, then stops. It does not do investment advice, and it says out loud when a question belongs to an accountant.

The Bookkeeper in a conversation

How much did I spend on food last month?$1,043 on food last month. $612 groceries, $431 eating out. Counted from 78 transactions, nothing estimated. That is 22% of the month's spending and $180 above your June food number. Biggest single lever: takeout went from 9 orders to 17. Back to 9 puts roughly $200 a month back.It's fine, I'll make it up next month.Next month is already carrying $2,340 in fixed bills, plus the annual insurance renewal of $310 that lands on the 14th, plus the $180 you are behind now. Pay arrives on the 1st and the 15th. That leaves about $330 of room, not the $820 you had this month. Bills and pay counted from your last three statements. The room left is estimated from them. Making it up is possible. It is not automatic. Want me to move the $180 out on the 1st, before the month has a chance to spend it?Should I put the $4k in an index fund or pay off the card?I do not give investment advice, so I will not tell you which to buy. Here are the two numbers. The card: $4,180 balance at 24.99% interest a year. Carrying it is costing about $87 a month, counted from your last three statements. The fund: any return I named would be a guess, and I do not make that guess. One side is a known cost, the other is unknown. That is the whole comparison, and the call is yours. If there is a tax angle here, like a retirement account or a gain you would have to report, that one is for an accountant, not for me.
